problems.source_says: The human-only arm is a two-person team that takes turns posting ideas in a shared panel, with the AI panel disabled. Its aid is the human partner. The form spec puts human partners under other_aid. The reconciled c052 form, which the c147 notes cite for this pairing, codes its no-AI team arm other_aid ('The human partner is the aid'), and c122 and c158 code their human-partner arms the same way. The c147 form also codes Individual-AI vs Human-only group as ai_vs_active, which codebook Section 5 defines as AI versus another aid such as 'a human partner'. So 'none' conflicts with the spec, with that precedent, and with the form's own contrast code. The arm should be other_aid. (c032 codes a no-AI dyad arm none, but there every arm is a dyad and no solo-AI arm is compared with it.) Criterion 1 does not change: the arm has no AI under either code, and Group-AI vs Human-only group stays ai_vs_bau, as c052 codes Team + AI vs Team No AI.
problems.quote: Following classic paradigms in the field of group creativity research, participants in both the group-AI condition and the human-only group condition generated ideas through a turn-taking interaction process.
problems.locator: p. 8, Section 2.2; p. 9, Figure 1 caption ('In the Human-Only Group condition, the AI invocation interface on the left was disabled'); form-spec.md, field note on arms[].ai; creativity-codebook.md, Section 5; forms/c052.json, arm 'Team No AI (T1)'

confirmed.statement: (a) Random pairing is stated: 'They were then randomly paired to form two-person teams.'

(a) Random assignment to conditions is stated: 'each team was randomly assigned to one of the three collaborative innovation conditions'. Read alone, this is between-team wording. But the same section says 'Each participant completed three experimental conditions', and the abstract and Section 2.1 call the design within-subject, so the random step can only set the order. The form's what_was_assigned and open_questions say this, and its assignment quote is verbatim.
confirmed.locator: pp. 7-8, Section 2.2; p. 1, Abstract ('Using a within-subject experimental design'); p. 7, Section 2.1

confirmed.statement: (e) The order of conditions is described as random. In Figure 1B, dashed arrows run from the three modes (Individual-AI, Group-AI, and Group Co-Creation) to 'Collaborative Innovation Model 1', '2', and '3' (15 min each, after a 5-min pre-test questionnaire), and they carry the label 'Random Presentation'. The prose says the order of conditions and the tasks 'were counterbalanced across participants to mitigate potential order and material confounds'. A random and a counterbalanced order are compatible. The procedure is not described, as the form says.

Unit within_person_order and structure within hold: 'The study employed a within-subjects experimental design with one factor'. Caveat, no code change: the order was set per team, so both partners share one sequence. The repeated-measures F(1, 47) tests of group-AI vs human-only group fit 48 pairs.

(b) What was assigned is access to ChatGPT-4o for the participant's own idea generation, not a change in whose output gets rated. Group-AI: each member 'was assigned their own AI tool', 'with only one opportunity to consult the AI by asking a single question related to the creativity task' per own turn. Individual-AI: 'participants collaborated one-on-one with the AI'. Human-only group: 'the AI invocation interface on the left was disabled'.

(c) The tool is a large language model: 'The AI system used was ChatGPT-4o, developed by OpenAI.' Figure 1A shows a prompt box ('Please Enter Your Prompt'), and the caption calls the left panel 'the ChatGPT-4o invocation interface'. name_model, role open_chat, and the generative_ai codes of the two AI arms are right.
confirmed.locator: p. 8, Section 2.2; p. 9, Figure 1A and caption

confirmed.statement: (d) Group-AI vs Human-only group = ai_vs_bau holds: both arms are pairs on a public panel, and only AI access differs. Individual-AI vs Human-only group = ai_vs_active holds under codebook Section 5 ('a human partner'): in individual-AI 'the right panel was set as a private communication platform where participants could only see their own input'.
confirmed.locator: p. 8, Section 2.2; p. 9, Figure 1 caption; creativity-codebook.md, Section 5

confirmed.statement: (d) Group-AI vs Individual-AI = ai_design is defensible. Both arms use ChatGPT-4o. They differ in the human partner, the public vs private panel, and the one-question-per-turn rule, which the text states only for group-AI. The learning screening calls a hybrid self/peer/AI arm vs direct AI an AI-design contrast although 'Conditions also change reflection, peer input, and workload'. The form's notes flag the contrast for Review 1.
confirmed.locator: p. 8, Section 2.2; p. 9, Figure 1 caption; docs/literature-screening-2026-09-23.md, line 31

confirmed.statement: Arm descriptions match the text: one idea per turn in QQ Chat, each group-AI member with their own AI tool, a private panel in individual-AI, the AI panel disabled in the human-only group, and 15 minutes per condition. n_analyzed = 96 per arm follows from 'a final sample of 96' and 'Each participant completed three experimental conditions'. n_randomized = null is right, because no count at assignment is printed.
confirmed.locator: p. 7, Section 2.1; p. 8, Section 2.2; p. 9, Figure 1

confirmed.statement: ai_tool.how_used counts match: 'After removing two prompts unrelated to the creativity tasks, a total of 209 prompts were collected from participants in the group-AI condition', and the authors coded 'all prompts collected from the individual-AI condition (n = 313)'. Participants 'either copied the AI’s idea verbatim or adapted it to create a new idea'.
confirmed.locator: p. 14, Section 2.5; p. 15, Section 2.5; p. 12, Section 2.4

confirmed.statement: design_class lab_rct holds: 'Upon arrival at the laboratory' and 'We employed a controlled laboratory design'. preregistered = not_stated holds: the text mentions no preregistration, only an a priori G*Power analysis (minimum of 56 participants). Elsewhere 'random' appears only for item selection ('three items were randomly selected') and for random effects.
confirmed.locator: p. 7, Sections 2.1-2.2; p. 6, Section 1; p. 10, Section 2.3; pp. 15-16, Section 3.1

confirmed.statement: Scope: this check covers the EdArXiv preprint on file (version 2, 31 pages). The 2026 JCAL version of record is not on file, so a changed description of the randomization there cannot be ruled out.

summary: Criterion 1 holds: the document says participants were 'randomly paired', that 'each team was randomly assigned' to the conditions, and Figure 1B labels the order of the three 15-minute conditions 'Random Presentation', so each person worked in a pair with ChatGPT-4o, alone with ChatGPT-4o, and in a pair without AI, in a random order (pp. 7-9). The coding is refuted on one detail: the human-only pair arm is coded none, but the form spec and the reconciled c052 form code a no-AI human-partner arm other_aid, and the form's own ai_vs_active code for Individual-AI vs Human-only group treats that partner as an aid.
